B: Hello? Hi.
A: Hi. Hello. I'm Maricel.
B: Luke. Sorry, can you say your name again? Just so I get it right.
A: Maricel. Like Mari, then cel.
B: Maricel. Got it. Sorry.
A: No, it's fine, everyone asks. Erm, so what do you do, Luke?
B: I'm a shift manager at a parcel depot. Basingstoke. Early shift.
A: Oh, okay. How early is early?
B: Half five start. So I'm up about quarter to five.
A: Oh God. I couldn't. I'm knackered after a normal Saturday shift.
B: You get used to it. Sort of. Yeah. What about you?
A: I'm a pharmacy technician. In a community pharmacy in Leyton. Checking prescriptions, care home medicines, that kind of thing.
B: Oh right. My mum works on reception at a GP surgery. She's always moaning about the repeat prescriptions.
A: Yes! Honestly, before a bank holiday it's chaos. Everyone remembers on the Thursday that they've got two tablets left, and the surgery hasn't sent it over, and then it's us they shout at. Not your mum, I'm sure she's lovely.
B: She'd say the same about you lot, to be fair. It's always someone else's fault in the middle, isn't it.
A: Mm. Exactly.
B: Bit like the depot. If a parcel goes missing, it's always the shift before.
A: Ha. And is it, though?
B: Sometimes it's mine. I'll own up if it is. Yeah.
A: That's good. A lot of people don't. Erm, do you like it? Being the manager?
B: Erm. Most of it. I like the people, I've got a good team. I don't like the bit where you've got to push 'em harder for targets, especially near Christmas. Peak season's horrible. I don't really sleep much in November, to be honest.
A: That sounds really stressful.
B: Yeah. It's alright. That's about it really.
A: Do you do anything to switch off?
B: Fishing, mostly. Carp. I sit by a lake all day on a Saturday and nobody can get hold of me. Caught a decent one last weekend actually.
A: I sort of get that. I do pottery, on the wheel. It's similar, maybe. You can't look at your phone with clay all over your hands. You just have to sit with it for two hours and not think about work.
B: Yeah, that's it. That's kind of the same thing, isn't it. Hannah, my girlfriend, she thinks fishing's boring.
A: My partner thinks pottery is just me making very expensive mugs. Which, to be fair, it is.
B: Ha. Do you go away much? Holidays and that?
A: Erm, Manila every other year, my family's there. And city breaks sometimes. But honestly, I'm terrible with flying. I plan everything weeks ahead, I check the gate three times, I don't sleep the night before.
B: Oh, me too. Hannah laughs at me. I like everything booked months in advance, and I'm at the airport like three hours early.
A: Three hours is normal!
B: That's what I keep telling her. We only go Tenerife, it's four hours, and I'm still—
